title: Canonical URL
content: A canonical URL is the representative URL selected for a page or a group of substantially duplicate pages.

meta.why: Competing versions of the same page can make reporting and internal linking harder to interpret.
meta.example: A product guide loads at a clean URL and again at a URL with campaign parameters, so the team declares the clean version as its canonical.
meta.check: Inspect the declared canonical and the Google-selected canonical in Search Console, then use the intended URL in internal links.
meta.limitation: A declared canonical is a signal, and Google can still choose a different representative URL.
meta.sources: Google Search Central: canonicalization | https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/canonicalization | Platform documentation
